matched_finding.subcategory: Invalid composite scoring of dependent variables
matched_finding.description: Invalid composite scoring of dependent variables: The authors propose creating a composite score for problematic substance use by averaging five items from the modified NIDA-ASSIST. However, three of these items are measured on a 0-5 scale, while the other two are measured on a 0, 3, 6 scale. Averaging items with different, unstandardized numerical ranges is mathematically invalid, as it arbitrarily weights the composite score toward the items with the larger numerical range. This will create a distorted dependent variable, undermining the validity of all subsequent moderation and equivalence tests for these behaviors.

matched_finding.description: Unspecified alternative statistical models: For a Registered Report, vaguely stating that supplemental analyses will be conducted if OLS assumptions are violated is insufficient. Given that the dependent variables (e.g., modified NIDA-ASSIST scores) measure problematic substance use in a general population, the data are highly likely to be right-skewed or zero-inflated. To prevent researcher degrees of freedom during the Stage 2 analysis, the authors must explicitly pre-specify the exact alternative models (e.g., negative binomial regression, zero-inflated Poisson, or robust standard errors) that will be employed if the assumptions of linearity, homoscedasticity, or normality of residuals are violated.

matched_finding.description: Contradictory survey routing logic: The manuscript contains a critical contradiction regarding the administration of the problematic use measures. On page 6, the text states that "only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use." However, on page 7, the text claims that "key measures will be administered to all participants regardless of their engagement in the behavior." This discrepancy fundamentally alters the sample size, degrees of freedom, and statistical distribution of the dependent variables. Including non-users will likely result in severe zero-inflation and heavily skew the interaction terms. Please clarify the exact inclusion criteria for the regression models and ensure the survey routing logic is consistently described.
